boardSettings.title: Public board
boardSettings.intro: The public board lets end-users see and vote on feedback you’ve approved. It’s off by default — no feedback is ever public until you enable the board and approve items in the moderation queue.
boardSettings.enableNote: When on, approved feedback is visible at your public board URL. Turning it off hides the board entirely (existing approvals are kept).
boardSettings.requireModerationNote: Always on in v1 — every item is reviewed before it can appear on the board. Auto-approve is reserved for a future release.

runnerTokens.title: Runner tokens
runnerTokens.explainer: A runner is an autonomous agent that polls for owner-approved work orders, runs them against your repository, and reports back. It authenticates with a short-lived runner write-token — a JWT you mint yourself from the private half of a registered runner-class key. feedbackmonk never holds your private key.
runnerTokens.securityNote: A runner token can drive a dispatched order but can never approve one — approval is an admin-only action (Contract C22). So even a fully compromised runner token cannot bypass your approval gate, which is why issuing them is safe to automate.

keyForm.heading: Register a runner key
keyForm.explainer: Generate an Ed25519 keypair on the runner host and register the public half here as a runner-class key. Unlike an identity key, a runner key can only verify runner write-tokens — it can never mint an end-user identity.
keyForm.publicKeyPlaceholder: base64 of the 32-byte raw Ed25519 public key
keyForm.registerFailed: Registration failed. The public key must be standard base64 of a 32-byte Ed25519 public key, and the label 1–100 characters.
keyForm.required: Both a label and a base64 public key are required.

tokenForm.heading: Register an issued token
tokenForm.explainer: Optional. After minting a token with <code1>feedbackmonk-runner mint-token</code1>, record its <code2>jti</code2> here so it appears in the list below and can be revoked. Registration is purely for visibility — a runner can authenticate whether or not its token is registered.
tokenForm.registerFailed: Registration failed. Check the jti and label (1–200 / 1–100 chars).
tokenForm.required: Both a token ID (jti) and a label are required.

runnerTokenCard.confirmRevoke: Revoke token “{{label}}”? This cannot be undone — the runner using it must mint a new token to keep working.

runnerTokensList.heading: Registered tokens
runnerTokensList.empty: No tokens registered yet. Registering a token here is optional — it only adds it to this list for visibility and revocation. A runner can authenticate the moment it mints a token from a registered runner key.
